title: Tools I like
text: These are tools I actually use and recommend to friends and family. Most are free. I’m not paid to mention any of them. If you’d like help setting one up, just ask.

title: Tools I like
text:
Staying safe online


 Bitwarden
A password manager that remembers strong, unique passwords for every site, on your computer and phone. Free for most people.
bitwarden.com


 Ente Auth
An app for the six-digit login codes (two-step login). Your codes are backed up, so a lost phone doesn’t lock you out.
ente.io/auth


 uBlock Origin
Blocks ads, pop-ups, and many scam sites in your web browser. Works best in Firefox. On Chrome, use uBlock Origin Lite.
ublockorigin.com


 Microsoft Defender
The antivirus already built into Windows. For most home users, it’s all you need, so you can skip the paid antivirus subscriptions. Look for “Windows Security” in the Start menu.

title: Tools I like
text:
Windows helpers


 WinDirStat
Shows what’s filling up your hard drive, as a colorful map, so you know what to clean up.
windirstat.net


 Everything
Finds any file on your computer instantly as you type. Much faster than the built-in Windows search.
voidtools.com

title: Tools I like
text:
Phones, maps, and the outdoors


 COTREX
Colorado’s official, free trail map app, with offline maps and fire alerts. Great for our local trails.
trails.colorado.gov


 CoMaps
Free offline maps and directions for anywhere in the world, with no ads or tracking.
comaps.app


 F-Droid
An app store for Android with free, open-source apps and no ads or tracking. A little more for the tinkerers.
f-droid.org

title: Tools I like
text:
Reading and watching


 Kanopy
Free movies and shows with your library card, on your TV, phone, or computer. Check whether your library participates.
kanopy.com


 RSS readers
Follow your favorite news sites and blogs in one place, without algorithms or social media. Feedly and Inoreader are easy places to start. I use FreshRSS with the FeedMe app.
What is RSS?

title: Scam help
text: Scams are getting more convincing, especially now that AI can fake voices and write perfect emails. I want everyone in Fruita to have someone local and trustworthy to call when something feels off.

title: Scam help
text:
Common warning signs


 It’s urgent
“Act now or your account will be closed.” Real companies give you time.


 Strange ways to pay
Gift cards, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, or a Bitcoin ATM. Those are almost always a scam.


 Pop-up “tech support”
A warning with a phone number to call about a virus. Microsoft and Apple don’t do that.


 A loved one in trouble
A call from a grandkid who needs bail money, in a voice that sounds just like them. AI can copy voices now. Hang up and call them back on their real number.

title: Scam help
section: If you think you’ve been scammed
text:
If you think you’ve been scammed
Don’t be embarrassed. It happens to smart, careful people every day.

Stop sending money or information, and don’t answer the scammer.
Call your bank using the number on the back of your card.
Call me. I can check your computer or phone, change passwords, and help lock things down.
Report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Protecting yourself ahead of time
See my favorite safety tools for the apps I recommend.

title: Hi, I’m Thomas!
text:
I’m the person behind Fruita Tech Wizard, and I live right here in Fruita.
My day job is Dynamodal, where I do data, AI, and energy analysis work for consulting teams. I enjoy that work, and I also wanted to do something for my own community, so I started FTW to offer friendly, personal tech help to my neighbors and local businesses.
I’ve always been the go-to tech person for family, friends, and coworkers. I studied physics and electrical engineering at the Colorado School of Mines, worked a few years in the Alaskan oil fields, and have spent the last couple of decades working with computers, data, and all the tech in between. I love explaining things in plain English and helping people feel more confident with their technology.
When I’m not working, I’m usually biking, running, or exploring the trails and rivers around Fruita.

Why FTW?
If you’ve spent any time in Fruita, you’ve probably seen the WTF stickers. Officially it stands for “Welcome to Fruita.” Unofficially… well, you know. (It even stirred up a little controversy.)
FTW is my nod to those stickers. It stands for Fruita Tech Wizard, and also “For The Win,” which is what I hope you’ll feel once your tech is working again. And the dino on a bike? That’s Fruita: dinosaurs and bikes.
